title: Secrets and Configuration with Key Vault

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of a managed identity?

options.text: It lets an app authenticate to services without any stored credentials
It stores your application's source code
It is a faster type of virtual machine

questions.explanation: A managed identity is an Entra ID identity for an Azure resource that lets it authenticate to services like Key Vault without any stored credentials to leak.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true about Key Vault and managed identities? Select all that apply.

options.text: Key Vault stores secrets, keys, and certificates
A system-assigned identity is tied to one resource; a user-assigned one is reusable
Key Vault references let App Service inject a secret into a setting at runtime
You should store non-secret settings and feature flags in Key Vault

questions.explanation: Key Vault holds secrets/keys/certs; system-assigned identities are tied to one resource, user-assigned are reusable; Key Vault references inject secrets at runtime. Non-secret settings belong in App Configuration.

questions.prompt: An automatically managed Entra ID identity for a resource, so it needs no stored password, is called a managed ____.
questions.explanation: A managed identity lets a resource authenticate as itself (system-assigned or user-assigned) with no credentials stored in code or config.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of the secure secret-access pattern.

items.text: Store the secret in Key Vault
Give the app a managed identity
Grant that identity access to the vault
The app reads the secret at runtime

questions.explanation: Store the secret, give the app an identity, grant that identity least-privilege access to the vault, and the app fetches the secret at runtime — no secret in code.

questions.prompt: Match each service or feature to its role.

pairs.right: Secure store for secrets, keys, and certificates
Centralized non-secret settings and feature flags
A setting that resolves to a vault secret at runtime

questions.explanation: Key Vault stores secrets; managed identities remove stored credentials; App Configuration holds non-secret settings; Key Vault references inject secrets into settings.
